payload.feature:
DSH COMPOSITE IDENTITY — issue #226 task 8.8 parts (a)–(c): the LAST macOS cell. Branch slice-dsh-composite-b; adopt every commit. One finding, narrow scope.

WHERE THIS STANDS. Run dsh-composite-identity-issue-226-d462f720 repaired eleven of the twelve macOS failures of PR #311; the PR's macOS leg now runs 373 passed, 1 failed. Every other check passes. The verbatim remaining failure is in .forge/tasks/controller-macos-ci-failures-pr311-pass2-2026-09-21.txt — READ IT FIRST. There is no macOS host here; that file is the only observation.

THE ONE. crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite/tests/native_matrix.rs:751, cell n1-l4 (both inherited and explicit), name "./dsh", layout "A:B, A is a self-symlink (ELOOP)". On macOS native fails with ELOOP (os error 62) and the resolver returns Err(Config("./dsh: Too many levels of symbolic links (os error 62)")) — the RAW error, without the named reason "a symlink loop stops the lookup" that the matrix requires whenever the terminal native errno is ELOOP. The same cell passes on Linux, and the n0 (searched-name) ELOOP rows pass on macOS. So on the Apple arm, a DIRECT name (one containing a slash) whose own path is a symlink loop is rendered through a path that skips the ELOOP naming. Find that path in composite.rs, find why the Linux arm names it and the Apple arm does not (the platform-qualified ELOOP rule — glibc terminal, Apple continues — applies to a SEARCH; a direct name has no search to continue, so ELOOP on a direct name is terminal on every platform), and make the direct-name refusal carry the named reason on every platform. Add a Linux-runnable unit test that drives the Apple library arm for a direct self-symlink name, as the existing per-library lookup table already does for searched names, so the fix is proved here and not only by the macOS leg. Prove by removal.

ALSO, the one LOW from run d462f720's chief, same file family: composite/tests.rs:7803 uses raw.symlink_metadata().is_err() — assert the specific cause (NotFound) or the directory's exact entry names instead. It is a macOS-only branch; make it compile on both hosts and say it awaits the macOS leg.

RULES. Every Linux string stays byte-identical. Assert reasons, never is_err(). No Windows handling (decision 0063). GATES, crate-scoped and sequential, never a boxed workspace run: fmt --check; clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings; every crate suite green; openspec validate --all --strict.

DO NOT TICK 8.8. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/, docs/decisions/ do not move. Record what you delivered and what awaits the macOS leg.

which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Read the pass-2 macOS transcript first. The one remaining failure (native_matrix.rs:751, cell n1-l4, ./dsh, self-symlink) came from lookup_failure applying the C library's SEARCH continuation switch to a DIRECT name: glibc and musl Stop on ELOOP and reach stop_cause, which names the loop, while Apple's posix_spawn switch Continues, so the candidate became Passed with only the raw io::Error. A direct name has no next entry, so ELOOP on it is terminal on every platform. Added a private Position { Searched, Direct } carried by classify_in and lookup_failure, and one guarded arm turning a Continue on ELOOP at a Direct position into stop_cause's named refusal. Scope is exactly the loop at a direct name: every library's Stop, every other continued errno at a direct name, and every searched candidate (including Apple's continuation past ELOOP to the next entry) are untouched, so every Linux string stays byte-identical. Proved on Linux, not only by the macOS leg: four new rows in the per-library lookup table (Direct+LOOP under Apple/glibc/musl give one identical named refusal; Direct+ENOENT/EACCES/EIO unchanged) plus a new test that plants a real a/dsh -> dsh self-symlink, confirms the host kernel answers ELOOP, and drives lookup_in with the direct path under an injected Library::Apple, Glibc, Musl and the compiled LIBRARY, each under Operation::Exec and Spawn, asserting the whole reason; ELOOP's rendering is derived from rustix Errno::LOOP, never Darwin's 62. The same test retains the searched controls. tests/native_matrix.rs unchanged. Removal proof recorded with both failure texts. The chief's LOW: the non-UTF-8 plugin-walk test now asserts ErrorKind::NotFound and the directory's exact entry names instead of is_err(); it compiles on both hosts and its filesystem-refusal arm awaits the macOS leg, since Linux tmpfs accepts the name.
